messages:
jordan: Heads-up: seeing a new class of funcall parse failures on pegasus-v2q int4 canary. ~2% of mirror requests with large metadata arrays are returning truncated JSON (missing trailing brace) and failing schema validation.

lia: Oof. Any correlation with seq length / packing? :thinking_face:

jordan: Yes. Spikes when total tokens > ~480. Repro locally by forcing a small kvcache margin. The stream ends mid-utf8 byte and JSON ends up cut.

oscar: Can you paste a dump (redact IDs)? small suffix would help.

jordan: Example truncated suffix (redacted):
```
..., "metadata": ["sensor_reading_123", "…", "47



```
Last item ends with no closing quote/bracket.

maya: Mirror-replay 5k sample: int4 canary 1.9% funcall_parse_failures vs float32 baseline 0.1%. Latency/cost still better for int4 but correctness regression too high to keep rollout.

sam: Could be token merger/batching boundary split or runtime kernel drop when buffer limit crossed.

jordan: Two hypotheses: (1) quant kernel tail clipping when buffer full (drops last bytes), (2) streaming flush before token commit for small batches. Both produce partial utf8/JSON suffix.

caro: Short-term mitigation: post-stream sanity check that validates last 64 bytes for UTF-8 validity and JSON-terminating chars. If invalid, append sentinel marker "\n\n<TRUNC_GUARD>\n\n" and flag for async-repair.

lia: We have a JSON-repair heuristic used by some toolcall adapters (closes braces/fixes quotes). We could enable it for this canary only and emit telemetry, but it risks masking real incomplete arguments.

oscar: Agree we should not auto-repair required schema fields (signature/intent). Conservative repair only for optional arrays like metadata. Can we gate by schema path?

jordan: Plan: 1) pause global rollout of pegasus-v2q int4, 2) enable conservative repair for optional leaf arrays, 3) increase kvcache margin + hold packing when seq_len > 420, 4) run 100k mirror A/B and collect parse_failures_by_schema_path.

maya: Telemetry to add: funcall_parse_failures, parse_repair_applied, repaired_fields (list), latency delta for repaired requests, and capture token window around boundary for kernel debugging.

sam: I'll add a runtime flag quant_tail_guard=true which pads outputs with a reserved sentinel token at end of generation to detect/avoid mid-byte drops. Low-risk toggle.

caro: Add canary alert: if parse failures > 0.5% sustained for 1 minute, auto-fail canary and revert to float baseline.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: enable quant_tail_guard on pegasus-v2q-canary. Rolling update across 6 nodes expected.

lia: Also add a unit test in runtime that simulates last-byte truncation after detokenize and assert JSON-repair heuristics never invent required fields (test must fail if required keys missing).

jordan: Action list: 
- jordan: draft test + run 100k mirror (ETA today EOD)
- sam: add quant_tail_guard flag + kvcache margin holdback (ETA 4h)
- caro: telemetry + canary alert (ETA 2h)
- lia: enable conservative repair for optional arrays (ETA 3h)
- maya: pause rollout & collect baseline snapshots (done)

maya: If mirror A/B yields <0.2% residual parse failures with repair+guard, we can consider gradual re-enable. Otherwise revert to float32 for canary. :thumbsup:

oscar: Ping me when token dumps are available. I want to instrument kernel entry to see where bytes vanish.

jordan: Dropping trace (redacted) at /infra/benchmarks/pegasus-v2q/trace-1779154321.log

caro: Filing a short postmortem-lite ticket and linking this thread. cc @eng-sre for rollback runbook.

sam: Good triage. Thanks everyone.

jordan: Will post A/B results here when complete.
